msg: warning: Variable j is a dead store!
reasoning: FALSE POSITIVE: d7e9711760a.c (Linux quota). Alarm fires at line 20 ('int i, j;'), condition True. 'j' is declared but never assigned or read anywhere in the function — it is an unused variable, not a dead store. A dead store requires an actual write whose value is never read; here there is no write to j at all. The tool incorrectly treats the declaration as a store. Simplification artifact.
